verses.text: The law is only a shadow of the good things coming, not the things themselves. So the same sacrifices, offered year after year, can never make those who come near perfect.
If they could, wouldn’t the sacrifices have stopped? The worshipers would have been cleansed once for all and would no longer feel guilty about their sins.
Instead, those sacrifices remind people of their sins every year.
It’s impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take sins away.
That’s why, when Christ came into the world, he said: “You didn’t want sacrifices and offerings, but you prepared a body for me.
You weren’t pleased with burnt offerings or sin offerings.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come to do your will, God; it’s written about me in the scroll.’”
First he says, “You didn’t want sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings, and you weren’t pleased with them”—even though the law required them.
Then he says, “Look, I have come to do your will.” He removes the first arrangement to establish the second.
By that will, we have been made holy through the offering of Jesus Christ’s body, once for all.
Every priest stands day after day doing his service and offering the same sacrifices again and again. Those sacrifices can never take sins away.
But after Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever, he sat down at God’s right hand.
Since then, he’s waiting until his enemies are put under his feet.
By one offering he has made perfect forever those who are being made holy.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First he says:
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts and write them on their minds.”
Then he adds: “I will no longer remember their sins and lawless acts.”
When these are forgiven, there’s no longer any need for an offering for sin.
So, brothers and sisters, we can enter the Most Holy Place with confidence because of Jesus’ blood.
He opened a new and living way for us through the curtain—that is, through his body.
And we have a great priest over God’s household.
So let’s come near with a sincere heart and complete confidence in faith. Our hearts have been cleansed from a guilty conscience, and our bodies have been washed with pure water.
Let’s hold tightly to the hope we confess without wavering, because the one who made the promise is faithful.
Let’s think about how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.
Let’s not stop meeting together, as some have made a habit of doing. Instead, let’s encourage one another, especially as you see the Day coming closer.
If we deliberately keep sinning after learning the truth, there’s no sacrifice for sins left.
There’s only a terrifying expectation of judgment and a raging fire ready to consume God’s enemies.
Anyone who rejected Moses’ law died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
How much worse punishment do you think someone deserves who tramples God’s Son, treats the covenant blood that made them holy as something ordinary, and insults the Spirit of grace?
We know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
It’s terrifying to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember those earlier days. After you received the light, you endured a hard struggle with suffering.
Sometimes you were publicly shamed and mistreated; other times you stood alongside people who were treated that way.
You showed compassion to me while I was in prison, and you gladly accepted the loss of your possessions, knowing you had something better and lasting in heaven.
So don’t throw away your confidence; it brings a great reward.
You need endurance, so that after doing God’s will, you’ll receive what he promised.
“In just a little while, the one who is coming will come and won’t delay.
But my righteous one will live by faith. If he pulls back, I take no pleasure in him.”
We aren’t among those who pull back and are destroyed. We are among those who trust God and are saved.
